chunks: And it is narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man gave another man one thousand dirhams as a muḍārabah investment, and he purchased his father with it while he did not know.
He عليه السلام said: “He is to be appraised, and if it exceeds by even one dirham, he is to be freed, and he is to work to repay the man’s wealth.”

key_terms.أَبَاهُ: his father, whose purchase triggers the legal consequence discussed
key_terms.أَلْفَ دِرْهَمٍ: one thousand dirhams given as the invested capital
key_terms.اسْتُسْعِيَ: he is required to work or strive to pay off the amount due
key_terms.مَالِ الرَّجُلِ: the man’s property or capital that must be restored
key_terms.مُضَارَبَةً: a profit-sharing investment arrangement in which one party provides capital
key_terms.يُقَوَّمُ: he is to be appraised or valued financially

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone unknowingly buys his own father through a muḍārabah investment?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a muḍārabah transaction in which a man unknowingly purchases his own father. The Imam عليه السلام rules that the father is to be appraised, and if the valuation exceeds by even one dirham, he is freed and made to earn toward repayment of the invested wealth.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3844 - It is narrated from Muhammad bin Qays who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (as), "A man gave another man one thousand dirhams in a partnership, and he unknowingly purchased his father with it."
Imam (as) said: "He should be valued, and if his value exceeds by even one dirham, he shall be freed and shall work to repay the man's wealth."
